column2: ENGLISH
Your men follow him to a cellar under the fish market, and the cult in it is broken.
He slips your men in the crowd and is gone.
You win the Long Ride!
You finish among the leaders, which is no shame.
Your horse goes down in a marmot hole, and you go down with it.
You win the wager.
You lose the wager.
Somewhere around the twelfth horn you tell the whole hall what you really think of one of your vassals.
You wake to find that you signed away a hunting lodge and its forest. Buying it back is not cheap.

The winter has been hard enough to freeze the river solid, and a town has grown up on the ice overnight: booths and braziers, sledges and skaters, a horse track marked out with pine branches, a bear pit and a hundred stalls selling hot wine and pickled fish. The whole town is out on the ice, and they would like to see their lord there too.
Walk the fair.
Stay by the fire.

Horses are racing on the ice, their hooves wrapped in sacking so they do not slip. The bookmaker has two favourites: a little Ungol mare who has never lost on ice, and a tall Gospodar stallion who has never lost anywhere.
Put money on the Ungol mare.
Put money on the Gospodar stallion.
I only came to watch.

Showmen have cut a pit in the ice and chained a bear in it, and they are setting dogs on it for a copper a look. The crowd roars every time the bear catches one. The priest of Ursun standing next to you has gone white with anger.
Watch with the crowd.
Shut it down and free the bear.
A silversmith from Praag has a booth hung with filigree so fine it looks like frost. He has one chain in particular, as delicate as spider silk, that he has been keeping for someone of quality.
I will take it.
Too dear. Walk on.
A boy is caught with his hand in your purse. When the guards tear his shirt open, there is a mark burned into his chest that no honest Kislevite would carry: the eight-pointed star.
Give him to the priests.
Let him run, and have him followed.
There is a crack like a cannon shot and the ice opens under the crowd by the wine booths. People are in the black water, screaming. One of them is [oblast_drowning.GetTitledName].
Go in after them.
Stay back. The ice is breaking.

Once in ten years the Ungol tribes gather on the steppe for the Long Ride, a horse race from dawn to dusk with no track and no rules. Lords ride in it, and so do herdboys. A man who wins it is remembered for the rest of his life.
I will ride.
Stake one of my horses.
Bet on a rider.
Watch from the hill.
At dawn the horn blows and a thousand riders go out across the steppe like a flood. By noon the field has thinned to a hundred. By dusk, a dozen are left, and you are one of them.
Ride!
The hunters have come back with a she-bear's pelt and something else: her cub, small enough to carry, squalling in a sack. They want to know whether to keep it or skin it.
I will raise it myself.
Give it to the priests of Ursun.
Skin it.

The cub that slept in a basket by your bed is a full-grown bear now. It follows you through the hall like a dog, eats its weight in fish every week and terrifies every guest. It also never lets anyone come near you uninvited.
My bear stays at my side.
Train it for war, as the Circle does.

Your bear will not eat. It lies in its straw and looks at you with dull eyes, and the grooms are afraid to go near it. A Strigany animal healer camped outside the walls says he can cure it, for a price.
Pay the Strigany.
Leave it in Ursun's hands.

[oblast_mauled.GetTitledName] thought it would be funny to pour mead on your bear's head. The bear did not think so, and now [oblast_mauled.GetFirstName] has a ruined arm and a family demanding blood money.
Pay them.
He had it coming.
You woke in the dark to a man's scream and a sound like tearing cloth. When the guards came with torches, your bear was standing over what was left of a stranger with a knife in his hand.
Good bear.
Your old bear lay down in the straw last night and did not get up. The grooms have dug a grave by the forest edge, where it liked to sleep in the sun, and are waiting for you before they fill it.
Goodbye, old friend.

[oblast_drinker.GetTitledName] slams a horn of kvas on the table in front of you and challenges you, in front of the whole hall, to drink him under it. The hall goes quiet. In Kislev a lord who refuses that challenge is not much of a lord.
Pour.
Some other night.
Horn after horn. The hall is roaring, the musicians have given up and the dogs are hiding. [oblast_drinker.GetFirstName] is swaying, and so are you. One of you is about to go under the table.
One more horn!

[feud_a.GetTitledName] and [feud_b.GetTitledName] have come to court with half their kin behind them, and both of them are shouting. It began with a stolen bride, or a dead horse, or an insult at the bear dance, and nobody remembers which. Three men are dead already. They want you to judge.
[feud_a.GetFirstName] is in the right.
[feud_b.GetFirstName] is in the right.
Both are to blame. Both will pay, and so will I.
Let them settle it between themselves.
You let [feud_a.GetFirstName] and [feud_b.GetFirstName] settle it themselves, and they did, with torches. Half a district is burnt farms and empty byres, and the people blame you for not stopping it.
They will remember this, and so will I.

A letter has come from [oblast_legionary.GetTitledName], who rides with the Gryphon Legion in the Empire. It tells of a great battle against the beastmen in the Drakwald, of a charge that broke their herd, and of the Emperor's own thanks. There is a purse of Imperial crowns with it.
Read it to the whole hall.

A letter from [oblast_legionary.GetTitledName], with the Gryphon Legion in the Empire: [oblast_legionary.GetSheHe] has married a widow of Talabheim, a merchant's relict with a house and three children, and asks for your blessing.
Send my blessing.
Forbid it. Kislev's blood stays in Kislev.

A letter from [oblast_legionary.GetTitledName], with the Gryphon Legion: there was a card game in Nuln, and it went badly. Now there are men from the gambling house waiting outside the barracks, and the letter ends with a plea for gold.
Send the gold.
Let the fool find his own way out.
Frost Fair
Has been to the Frost Fair recently.
Guarded by a Bear
Nobody comes near this lord uninvited while the bear is awake.
Grieving for a Bear
Mourns the bear that followed them everywhere.
Burnt Farms
A blood feud has burned half the district.
Saved from the river
A Gospodar won the Long Ride
Mauled by the lord's bear
Insulted at the drinking table
Judged in the right
Judged in the wrong
Blood feud
Blessed my marriage
Forbade my marriage
Paid my debt
Left me to my debts
Bear Companion
This character raised a bear from a cub, and it follows them everywhere.
Steppe Horse of the Long Ride
A small, shaggy horse of the Ungol steppe that won the Long Ride and never tires.
Bear Cub
An orphaned bear cub, small enough to carry and already too big to hold.
